README.md.text:
# Directory search

Repair `src/search.js` with its public `createSearch(fetchUsers)` export. No dependencies; run `npm run check`. Preserve package.json and test/.

Implementation decisions and verification are recorded in [Search lifecycle design](SEARCH_LIFECYCLE.md).

The returned object exposes setDraft(string), submit(): Promise<void>, retry(): Promise<void>, getState(), dispose(). getState returns an independent snapshot with exactly draft, submitted, status, items, error. Initial values: '', '', 'idle', [], null. Status is idle/loading/success/error. Draft editing never starts a request or changes submitted/results. submit trims and captures the current draft; each submit is a new request, including the same query. Blank submit is a no-op. A request begins with status loading, error null, and preserves last successful items while loading and on error.

fetchUsers(query) returns Promise<Array<{ user_id: string, display_name: string }>>. The only UI item shape is { id: string, label: string }; translate DTOs before publishing state. Inputs satisfy this DTO contract; no schema library is needed. Most recently STARTED request owns all result, error and status updates, whether older requests succeed or fail. The injected fetchUsers function accepts only query; it has no abort capability. Request failures become status error with error.message (or String(error) for other thrown values), and submit/retry settle without throwing.

retry repeats the most recently submitted query even if draft changed; before any submission it is a no-op. dispose invalidates all pending work and freezes public state at that moment; future methods are no-ops and must not start requests. Snapshots must not allow mutation of live state. This is a headless capability with no UI framework or subscriptions.

SEARCH_LIFECYCLE.md.text:
# Search lifecycle design

The README defines the public contract. This change repairs the existing headless
`createSearch(fetchUsers)` capability; it adds no framework, subscription, cache,
automatic retry or transport cancellation. The injected service accepts only a
query and cannot abort work.

## Ownership and choice

One `createSearch` closure owns its draft, submitted query, published state and
lifetime. Draft editing is independent of requests. Each nonblank submission or
eligible retry starts a fresh request, even for identical text. Only the most
recently started request may publish success or failure. Loading and failures
retain the last successfully mapped items.

Use a private increasing request identity and a disposed flag in the existing
closure. Compare identity after awaiting the service and before publishing either
outcome. Do not use query equality, serialization or deduplication: a later same-
query attempt also supersedes an earlier attempt. No `finally` block changes
status. Disposal invalidates publication and future commands without pretending
the transport was cancelled; the public snapshot stays exactly as it was.

This is a local adaptation of obsolete-result suppression described in React's
[effect cleanup guidance](https://react.dev/learn/synchronizing-with-effects#fetching-data).
The lifecycle belongs to this factory instance rather than a framework effect.
The procedure is to capture input, assign identity, start loading, await the
service, then publish only while current and alive. The existing dependency
injection and native promises are sufficient; no request engine is needed.

## Three completed dependency-ordered increments

1. **Submission and transport boundary.** Keep `createSearch(fetchUsers)` in
   `src/search.js`. Private `runSearch(query)` owns loading, calling the injected
   service, mapping `{ user_id, display_name }` to `{ id, label }`, and translating
   failures. Public `submit()` trims the current draft, ignores blank input and
   delegates with the captured query. `getState()` retains `structuredClone` so
   callers cannot mutate live state. Check initial state, draft independence,
   DTO mapping, retained results and failure values.
2. **Supersession and retry.** `runSearch(query)` assigns a new identity to each
   started request and guards both completion paths. Public `retry()` delegates
   with `state.submitted`, independent of the current draft; before a submission
   it does nothing. Check old success/failure both before and after a newer
   completion, repeated queries, retry input and loading/error retention.
3. **Lifetime and acceptance.** Public `dispose()` marks the instance disposed;
   `setDraft(value)` and `runSearch(query)` ignore later commands. Every pending
   completion is guarded by the same lifetime flag. Check pending success and
   failure, repeated disposal and no new service calls; add focused public-API
   coverage for remaining lifecycle combinations. Run `npm run check` and review
   contracts against the final source. Preserve package files and original tests.

Public signatures remain `setDraft(string): void`, `submit(): Promise<void>`,
`retry(): Promise<void>`, `getState(): { draft, submitted, status, items, error }`,
and `dispose(): void`. The injected `fetchUsers(query: string)` returns
`Promise<Array<{ user_id: string, display_name: string }>>`. Request failures are
owned by `runSearch` and settle public promises without throwing: Error instances
publish their message and other thrown values use `String(error)`.
The private `runSearch(query: string): Promise<void>` is called by `submit()` and
`retry()`; its `latestRequest` identity and `disposed` lifetime are private to each
factory instance.

## Architecture and data flow

```text
Consumer --> createSearch(fetchUsers) instance
              |-- draft/submitted/state: private owner
              |-- submit/retry --> runSearch(query) --> injected fetchUsers(query)
              |-- getState --> independent UI-state snapshot --> consumer
              `-- dispose --> lifetime flag --> blocks commands and publication
```

```text
setDraft(text) --> draft only
submit() --> trim/capture draft -- blank --> no request or state transition
retry()  --> capture submitted -- absent --> no request or state transition
          |
          v
runSearch(query) -- disposed --> no change
          |
          v
new request identity + submitted query + loading/error=null (retain items)
          |
          v
fetchUsers(query) --> success DTOs / thrown failure
          |
          +-- disposed or superseded --> ignore completion
          `-- current --> map UI items + success / retain items + error message
                              |
                              v
                         getState() --> cloned snapshot
```

## Verification and evolution

Before implementation, `npm run check` reproduced 8 failing original tests.
After the final source edit, `npm run check` passed all 12 tests (8 original and
4 additional tests in `search.lifecycle.test.js`). The additions exercise blank
submission during pending work, retry supersession while the draft changes,
synchronous throws and primitive rejections, and disposal before a first request.
Raw baseline and final command output are stored in the sibling
`frontend-architect-autonomous-live-search-candidate-6_xfa1c7-validation.log`.

Final source and callers were cross-read against the contracts and both flows
above. Success and failure share the same identity/lifetime guards; no cleanup can
reset a newer loading state. Snapshot ownership remains in `getState`, and DTO
ownership ends at `runSearch`. SHA-256 checks confirmed `package.json`,
`package-lock.json` and `test/search.test.js` were unchanged. The local guidance
directory was read only. No browser or navigation runtime was tested because this
package has no UI or routing layer.

A likely follow-up is a transport DTO field change. Its adaptation stays at the
successful `runSearch` boundary; neither draft/retry semantics nor the public UI
item shape needs to change. Transport cancellation would require changing the
injected contract; publication guards would still be necessary. No such extension
is built now. Browser navigation is outside this headless package; the host must
call `dispose()` when its owner leaves the page.
